open_questions: Could high-impact bimodal transits of a grazing EB partially reproduce the flat-bottom shape?
dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate between shallow and deep with large depth scatter between individual transits and strong out-of-eclipse variability on this spotted M dwarf. This pattern matches an eclipsing binary at twice the reported period viewed through a blend, not a stable planetary transit.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits have very different depths, favouring a binary at twice the period (11.4 d) with alternating primary/secondary eclipses rather than a single planet period.

Individual transit depths are extremely inconsistent, with one flat/negative event and two ~2-3x deeper events carrying the signal. This is not consistent with a steady planet transit and points to a blend/variable eclipse.
reasons.value: p_consistent 1.927214641401554e-26, chi2 122.79731833528766 dof 3, share_of_top_3 1.0, depths -3053 ppm, 41709 ppm, 55535 ppm vs mean 21277 ppm; reflit snr 18.62 transits 3 share 0.5421

reasons.why: Significant out-of-eclipse modulation at the signal period supports a close eclipsing binary/spotty blend over a quiet planetary transit, alongside the odd/even and depth scatter.

The star is a highly variable active M dwarf (31142 ppm rotation amplitude), near the duration period 5.68 d, with fit_density_penalty 2.461, increasing likelihood the signal is variability/blend rather than a planet on this small star.
reasons.value: rotation_d 9.763, signal_over_rotation 0.5813766260370787, false_alarm 1.090668051353543e-08 amplitude_ppm 31142, stellar rad 0.3503 Rsun Teff 3421 K
